author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: 1Password has no syslog or webhook for these events, so these parsers read records pulled from the 1Password Events API by the example bridge in bridges/1password-events and posted to HTTP Ingest. The bridge names each record's feature in onepassword_record. Sign-in attempts go to Auth, with the category (success, credentials_failed, mfa_failed, sso_failed, firewall_failed and others) as the result and the type as the detail. Item usage (reveal, fill, secure-copy, export, share and server changes) and audit events (vault, group, user, MFA, SSO and firewall changes) go to CloudAudit; an audit event's name is its object type and action, such as user.suspend. Samples follow the object shapes in 1Password's Events API reference with made-up values. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (138 of 138 fields matched the emulator, including a nanosecond and an offset timestamp), and the parent's confirm string picked the same records there. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent. No built-in parser claimed these records in 10 Run Tests.
